paragraph: [The central bank reported that 31.54% of the population held at least one bank account in 2024](<https://diariodosnegocios.com/inclusao-financeira-angola-desafios-bancarizacao-2024/>), up 0.76 points on 2023. In December 2025 the Minister of State for Economic Coordination [put the share of the population with a bank account at 31%](<https://afi-global.org/news/angolas-national-financial-inclusion-strategy-aims-to-boost-economic-and-social-development/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. The central bank does not say its figure comes from a survey, and no survey since 2023 has been found. Establishing would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 53% or more.

In November 2026 the director of the national financial inclusion agency [put the overall rate of use of financial services at 81.8% at the end of 2025](<https://lefaso.net/spip.php?article150583=>). In the last twelve months the rate rose from [79.7% at the end of 2024, which C’Finance reported](<https://cfinance.news/article/inclusion-financiere-avec-797-a-fin-2024-le-burkina-en-avance-de-61-points-sur-le-taux-global-de-luemoa/>). The agency does not say the rate comes from a survey. No survey found gives the share of adults who made or received a digital payment. Mature would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults who made or received a digital payment at 79% or more.

[FinScope's 2024 survey found that 75% of Batswana use mobile money, TechCabal reported in September 2026](<https://techcabal.com/2026/09/16/botswana-future-of-banking-not-start-with-bank/>). A mobile money account counts as an account. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No survey found gives the share of adults holding either a bank or a mobile money account, or the share who made or received a digital payment. Operating would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 79% or more.

[World Bank Global Findex puts Côte d'Ivoire's financial inclusion rate at 58% in 2024, up from 41% in 2017](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-finances/0910-59598-cote-d-ivoire-seeks-to-diversify-fintech-sector-beyond-digital-payments>). [The regulator ARTCI's 2024 survey found 50.3% of people aged five and over with a personal mobile money account](<https://www.artci.ci/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Rsum_Excutif_MSI_2024_200226.pdf>). That base includes children, so it is not a share of adults. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No survey found since 2023 puts adults with an account at 79% or more. Operating would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 79% or more.

[The World Bank's Global Findex puts account ownership among Cameroonian adults at 60.87% in 2024](<https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/FX.OWN.TOTL.ZS?locations=CM>). The figure counts accounts at a financial institution or a mobile money provider. No later survey of Cameroonian adults has been found, and no change has been found in the last twelve months. No survey found gives the share of adults who made or received a digital payment. Operating would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 79% or more.

No stage is set. The newest figure found, Global Findex for 2022, puts formal account ownership at nearly 39%. It is older than three years, so it does not count against the test. No survey since 2023 gives a share of adults with an account. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 53% or more.

[The Banco de Cabo Verde’s 2025 payment system report put the banking rate at 85.6%](<https://expressodasilhas.cv/economia/2026/09/25/mais-cabo-verdianos-com-contas-bancarias-e-maior-uso-de-pagamentos-digitais/104797>). The rate is the share of the resident population holding a current or payment account. In the last twelve months the rate rose from 81.5% in 2024, Expresso das Ilhas reported in September 2026. The report does not say the figure comes from a survey. No survey found gives the share of adults who made or received a digital payment. Mature would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults who made or received a digital payment at 79% or more.

No stage is set. The only figure found is the central bank governor's 36% of the population with bank account access, given in November 2024. It is not attributed to a survey and is not limited to adults. No survey share of adults with an account has been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 53% or more.

[A presentation of Global Findex data put Algerian adults with an account at 35.3% in 2024](<https://maghrebemergent.news/fr/les-chiffres-lattestent-lepargne-dort-un-potentiel-inexploite/>), Maghreb Emergent reported in April 2026. [La Voix de l’Algérie gave the Findex rate as 35%](<https://lavoiedalgerie.dz/selon-global-findex-2025-le-numerique-ouvre-de-nouvelles-perspectives-pour-la-finance-en-algerie/2025/12/00/>). [The same report puts adults who made or received a digital payment at 13%](<https://lavoiedalgerie.dz/selon-global-findex-2025-le-numerique-ouvre-de-nouvelles-perspectives-pour-la-finance-en-algerie/2025/12/00/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No survey has been found that puts adults with an account at half or more. Establishing would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 53% or more.

[Global Findex 2025 puts Egyptian adults with a formal account at 43%](<https://www.alborsaanews.com/2025/07/21/1902282>), Al Borsa News reported in July 2025. The survey year is 2024. In the last twelve months the Central Bank of Egypt [put its financial inclusion rate at 79% at the end of June 2026](<https://www.businesstodayegypt.com/Article/1/8078/Egypt%E2%80%99s-financial-inclusion-rate-rises-to-79-in-June-2026>), up from 77.6% at the end of 2025. The bank’s rate counts people with accounts and is not a survey. No survey has been found that puts adults with an account at half or more. Establishing would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 53% or more.

[A 2025 paper citing Global Findex puts account ownership among Ethiopian adults at 49% in 2024](<https://doi.org/10.51244/ijrsi.2025.1210000333>). The same paper gives 22% for 2014 and 35% for 2017. [The National Bank of Ethiopia put adults with a bank account at about 45% in 2020](<https://blogs.worldbank.org/en/nasikiliza/leveraging-e-payments-financial-inclusion-ethiopia-afe-0324>). No change has been found in the last twelve months, and no survey found since 2024 gives a higher share. Establishing would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 53% or more.

The GSMA's [October 2026 report on Gabon](<https://www.gsma.com/newsroom/all-documents/gsma-calls-for-more-affordable-smartphones-as-over-half-of-gabons-population-remains-off-mobile-internet-despite-network-coverage/>) says 62% of adults hold a mobile money account. It does not name the survey behind the figure. An earlier report put [about 54% of adults unbanked](<https://www.biometricupdate.com/202512/gabon-pens-deal-with-uncdf-to-accelerate-financial-inclusion>) in the World Bank's Global Findex 2025, which leaves about 46% with a bank account. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No survey puts account holding at four in five adults. Operating would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 79% or more.

In November 2026 the Governor of the Bank of Ghana said that [recent global surveys put about 81% of Ghanaian adults as owning a financial account](<https://www.bog.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Opening-Remarks-by-Governor-Dr-Johnson-Pandit-Asiama-at-the-11th-Meeting-of-the-Payment-Systems-Advisory-Committee-PSAC-021126.pdf>). In November 2026 [Citi Newsroom reported that the Deputy Minister of Finance cited Global Findex 2025 at above 80%](<https://www.citinewsroom.com/2026/11/financial-inclusion-expands-but-economic-well-being-remains-low-at-22/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No survey found gives the share of Ghanaian adults who made or received a digital payment. Mature would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults who made or received a digital payment at 79% or more.

In July 2026 the central bank [put the account access rate at nearly 36% in 2024, up from 4% in 2011](<https://www.africaguinee.com/inclusion-financiere-la-bcrg-realigne-sa-strategie-nationale-sur-les-ambitions-de-simandou-2040/>). Its first deputy governor gave the figure at a meeting of central banks in Luanda. The central bank does not say the figure comes from a survey. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and no survey share of adults with an account has been found. Establishing would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 53% or more.

No stage is set. In 2025 FinScope found 82% of adults with access to formal financial services. That is an inclusion share and not a share of adults with an account. No survey found since October 2023 gives the share of adults with an account. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 79% or more.

In September 2026 the national director of the regional central bank, the BCEAO, [put the overall access rate to financial services at 79.5% at the end of 2025](<https://www.odemocratagb.com/?p=59036>). The rate was 20.5% in 2018. She said the rise came mainly from electronic money. The bank does not say the rate comes from a survey. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No survey found gives the share of adults who made or received a digital payment. Mature would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults who made or received a digital payment at 79% or more.

[The Central Bank of Kenya's 2024 FinAccess Household Survey puts formal financial access at 84.8% of adults](<https://www.centralbank.go.ke/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/2024-FINACCESS-HOUSEHOLD-SURVEY-MAIN-REPORT.pdf>). It was 83.7% in 2021. Formal access means an active account in the adult's own name with a bank, a mobile money provider or a SACCO. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No survey found gives the share of Kenyan adults who made or received a digital payment. Mature would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults who made or received a digital payment at 79% or more.

[Finance Minister Augustine Ngafuan, citing the World Bank's Global Findex, said Liberia reached 52% account ownership by 2024](<https://www.thenewdawnliberia.com/liberia-expands-digital-finance/>). The New Dawn reported the statement in July 2026. Findex is a survey of adults. No later survey of Liberian adults has been found, and no change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 53% or more.

[Bank Al-Maghrib's 2024 financial-inclusion report cites the Global Findex 2024 survey: 44% of Moroccan adults hold a bank or payment account](<https://www.bkam.ma/content/download/844040/9139542/Rapport%20annuel%20sur%20l'Inclusion%20financière%202024.pdf>). [The same report puts its own bank account holding rate at 58% at the end of 2024, up from 53% in 2021](<https://www.bkam.ma/content/download/844040/9139542/Rapport%20annuel%20sur%20l'Inclusion%20financière%202024.pdf>). That rate counts residents with an active bank account, and is not a survey. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 53% or more.

[AfricaNenda's 2025 consumer deck for Madagascar cites Global Findex 2025](<https://africanenda.org/wp-content/uploads/Consumer-Deck_Madagascar_SIIPS-2025_compressed.pdf>): 24% of adults own a formal account. The deck was published in November 2025, and [it puts adults who used digital payments in the past year at 22%](<https://africanenda.org/wp-content/uploads/Consumer-Deck_Madagascar_SIIPS-2025_compressed.pdf>). In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. No other survey of Malagasy adults since 2023 has been found. Preparing would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 26% or more.

[A Banco de Moçambique report cites Global Findex 2025: 46% of adults hold an electronic money account and 25% a traditional bank account](<https://www.bancomoc.mz/media/nvelycjp/relatorio-inclusao-finaceira-maio031025pt-f.pdf>). The survey was face to face, from 15 October to 16 December 2024. It left out Cabo Delgado and some other districts, about 11% of the population. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No share of adults holding either a bank or an electronic money account has been found. Establishing would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 53% or more.

No stage is set. The newest figure found is a 2021 COMESA report of 90% of adults with a bank account. It is older than three years. No survey since 2023 gives a share of adults with an account. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Mature would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults who made or received a digital payment at 79% or more.

[The Bankers Association of Malawi's chief executive said in July 2025 that Global Findex 2025 puts adults with a financial account at 50% in 2024](<https://mwnation.com/banks-respond-to-digital-services-demand-bam/>). [FinScope's 2023 survey of 3,000 adults found 69% currently using mobile money and 13% banked](<https://finmark.org.za/Publications/2023_FinScope_Consumer_Survey_Malawi_2023_Report.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No survey found puts adults with an account at 53% or more. Establishing would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 53% or more.

[The Namibia Statistics Agency's 2025 Financial Inclusion Survey found 75.6% of adults aged 15 and over with a bank account](<https://nsa.org.na/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/2025-Namibia-Financial-Inclusion-Survey-Report.web_.pdf>). It puts adults with a smart card account at 18.3%. [World Bank economist Leora Klapper said in October 2025 that Global Findex 2025 puts Namibian adults with a financial account at 73%](<https://thebrief.com.na/2025/10/most-namibians-struggle-to-access-emergency-funds-world-bank/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No survey found gives the share of adults holding a bank or smart card account together. Operating would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 79% or more.

[NITDA's Nigeria Tech Outlook Report 2026, launched on 11 November 2026, says 86.5% of adults hold financial accounts](<https://von.gov.ng/nitda-unveils-nigeria-tech-outlook-report/>). It names neither bank nor mobile money accounts. In the last twelve months [EFInA's survey, released on 16 September 2026, put formal financial inclusion at 73% of adults](<https://independent.ng/nigerias-financial-inclusion-reaches-79-as-efinas-a2f-2026-survey-points-to-next-challenge/>), up from [64% for 2023](<https://a2f.ng/a2f-2026-making-financial-inclusion-work-harder-for-nigerians/>). [EFInA, reading the 2025 Global Findex, says 54% of Nigerian adults make digital payments](<https://efina.org.ng/2025/08/28/beyond-access-turning-financial-inclusion-into-financial-resilience-in-nigeria/>). Mature would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults who made or received a digital payment at 79% or more.

In June 2024 the Ministry of Finance launched FinScope 2024. It [found 77% of adults holding a registered mobile money account, up from 60% in 2020](<https://www.minecofin.gov.rw/news-detail/96-of-rwandans-are-financially-included-finscope-survey-2024>), and 22% banked. In the last twelve months the survey was cited and not changed: [KT Press reported FinScope at 73% of adults using services such as mobile money](<https://www.ktpress.rw/2025/12/new-survey-reveals-consumer-digital-fraud-risks-in-rwanda/>) in December 2025. No survey found since October 2023 puts adults with an account at 79% or more. Operating would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 79% or more.

No stage is set. A FinScope survey of 2021 found 15% of adults banked. It is the newest survey found and is older than three years. No survey since 2023 gives a share of adults with an account. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 26% or more.

[The BCEAO's national director said in July 2024 that Senegal's financial inclusion rate reached 83.3% in 2023, up from 61.9% in 2016](<https://www.orbit.sn/le-taux-dinclusion-financiere-du-senegal-est-superieur-a-la-moyenne-de-la-zone-uemoa-selon-le-directeur-national-de-la-bceao/>). The rate is the share of adults with a bank, postal, treasury, microfinance or e-money account. The BCEAO does not say the rate comes from a survey. No change has been found in the last twelve months, and no survey of Senegalese adults since 2023 has been found. Mature would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults who made or received a digital payment at 79% or more.

[The WTO's 2025 trade policy review summary says only about 29% of adults in Sierra Leone have an account](<https://www.wto.org/english/tratop_e/tpr_e/s470_sum_e.pdf>). The account may be with a formal financial institution or a mobile money provider. The figure names no survey and no year. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found puts adults with an account at over half, or gives the share paying digitally. Establishing would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 53% or more.

[An opinion piece on the Somalia Financial Access Survey 2026 puts mobile money reach at 87% of adults](<https://www.dawan.africa/news/opinionsomalias-financial-inclusion-story-beyond-access-to-economic-resilience>). The Central Bank of Somalia launched the survey in July 2026. The Somali Microfinance Association reported that [it found 90% of adults financially included, largely through mobile money](<https://www.linkedin.com/posts/somali-microfinance-association-somma_somma-somalia-financialinclusion-activity-7488596234996371457-auqx>). In the last twelve months the bank ran the country's first nationally representative survey of financial access. No survey found gives the share of adults who made or received a digital payment. Mature would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults who made or received a digital payment at 79% or more.

No stage is set. A UNDP report says under 6% of adults held an account in 2021. That is the newest figure found, and it is older than three years. No survey since 2023 gives a share of adults with an account. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 26% or more.

[The central bank's second demand-side survey on financial inclusion and literacy, run in early 2025, found 38% of adults with a bank account](<https://afi-global.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Relatorio_lado_da_procura-Final-PT.pdf>). The Alliance for Financial Inclusion published the report in February 2026. The survey counts bank accounts alone, without mobile money. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No survey share of adults with a mobile money account, or with any account, has been found. Establishing would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 53% or more.

[The Times of Eswatini reported in August 2025 that Global Findex 2025 puts 63% of adults with an account at a financial institution or a mobile money provider](<https://www.times.co.sz/business/readmore.php?bhsadjgfoh=Mobile+money+drives+financial+inclusion+growth&bvhdgsj=Business+and+Economy&yiphi=435>). Findex is a World Bank survey of adults. No later survey of adults in Eswatini has been found, and no change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 79% or more.

No stage is set. An Afrobarometer survey of March 2022 found 78% of adults with a mobile money account. It is the newest survey found and is older than three years. No survey since 2023 gives a share of adults with an account. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 79% or more.

[Global Findex puts Tunisian adults with an account at a financial institution or mobile money service at 37.8% in 2024](<https://www.challenges.tn/economie/bancarisation-en-tunisie-moins-de-comptes-plus-dagences-quel-cap/>), Challenges reported in November 2026. [Findex 2021 put it at 37%](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099040002202354875/pdf/IDU010adfdbe08bd3044f808e620311d82b11461.pdf>), unchanged from 2017. In the last twelve months the number of bank accounts [fell 1.8% to 10.5 million in 2025](<https://www.challenges.tn/economie/bancarisation-en-tunisie-moins-de-comptes-plus-dagences-quel-cap/>). No survey has been found that puts adults with an account at half or more. Establishing would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 53% or more.

[The Citizen reported in September 2026 that the FinScope Tanzania 2023 survey put mobile money adoption at 72%, up from 60% in 2017](<https://www.thecitizen.co.tz/tanzania/news/national/mobile-money-surge-fuels-cashless-growth-5578364>). A mobile money account counts as an account. No newer survey of Tanzanian adults has been found, and no change has been found in the last twelve months. No survey found gives the share of adults holding a bank or mobile money account. Operating would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 79% or more.

[FSD Uganda, quoting Global Findex 2025, says 73% of Ugandan adults have a financial account](<https://fsduganda.or.ug/connected-but-not-included/>). The survey year is 2024. [FinScope Uganda 2023 found 64% registered for mobile money](<https://ufla.co.ug/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Final-Finscope-Uganda-2023-Survey.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No survey has been found that puts account holding at 79% or more. Operating would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 79% or more.

[The payments group ASAPP, citing FinMark Trust's FinScope surveys of 2024 and 2025, says 89% of South African adults have a bank account](<https://marketingspread.co.za/payment-challengers-move-from-consultation-to-action-with-proposals-for-sas-payments-future-2/>). Marketing Spread published the statement in September 2026. The figure counts bank accounts alone, without mobile money. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No survey found gives the share of South African adults who made or received a digital payment. Mature would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults who made or received a digital payment at 79% or more.

[ITWeb reported in July 2026 that Bank of Zambia figures from the 2025 FinScope survey put mobile money usage at 76.2%](<https://www.itweb.co.za/article/from-rails-to-routine/dgp45vaB8nQ7X9l8>). [The same figures put financial inclusion at 80.1%, up from 69.4% in 2020](<https://www.itweb.co.za/article/from-rails-to-routine/dgp45vaB8nQ7X9l8>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No survey found gives the share of adults holding a bank or mobile money account. Operating would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 79% or more.

No stage is set. A FinScope Zimbabwe survey of 2022 found 70% of adults with an account. It is the newest survey found and is older than three years. No survey since 2023 gives a share of adults with an account. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need a survey from the past three years that puts adults with an account at 79% or more.
